answer: An agent economy resists Sybils by requiring each identity to bind a unique kernel proof to a non-clonable basalt-derived hardware measurement. The agent generates a VDF chain starting from its enclave's basalt fingerprint mixed with a public epoch challenge; peers recompute the final umber-tinted commitment hash. Cloning demands a fresh enclave per alias because the basalt measurement is physical and non-exportable, so each extra sybil costs a new secure hardware unit plus the VDF compute time, while an honest agent reuses one kernel. Bonds are slashed if the umber verification fails.
